samples.text: Floating-point numbers have limited precision, which causes rounding errors when representing real numbers. When adding three numbers, the order of operations can determine which intermediate sums are rounded, changing which values are lost to rounding error. Therefore, (a + b) + c can produce a different result than a + (b + c) because the rounding occurs at different points in the calculation.

These different intermediate values then lead to different final results due to subsequent rounding.
